Independent exhaustive nonsplit binary unit-surjectivity checks at 7 primes p≡1 mod3 through 61, across all ordered nonsplit unit coefficient pairs, plus all 27 possible cubic-coset configurations; universal conclusion remains Hasse/Hensel.
correctness.rationale: Local variable scaling normalizes valuations mod3. If the repeated pair is split, a simple binary zero yields an open ball of represented values and all local quotients. If nonsplit and p=1 mod3, the smooth genus-one curve alpha X^3+beta Y^3=tZ^3 has an F_p-point by Hasse, no points at infinity because -beta/alpha is not a cube, so a nonsingular affine point lifts by Hensel to every p-adic unit t. Binary values represent all unit parts in valuation 0 mod3, while the third term at exponent k=1 or2 enables all quotient valuation residues 0,k,-k. When all valuations agree the ternary smooth-zero lemma gives local quotients; when distinct the minimum summand is unique, higher terms lie in 1+pZ_p=(Z_p×)^3 for p!=3, so value cosets and pairwise ratios have the exact group-difference geometry. p=2 is covered since all units are cubes. Integer vectors approximate local vectors and continuity of nonzero denominators gives density. Independent finite checks exhaust nonsplit pairs at seven p=1 mod3 primes <=61 and all 27 F3² quotient-coset configurations.
residual_risks: Local equality R(F(Q_p^3))=Q_p is not equality with the integer-coordinate quotient set; only density is proven there.
The theorem excludes p=3, non-diagonal or non-homogeneous forms.

Their distinct-valuation case and a general coset result are prior-covered. The present nonsplit mixed-valuation density is not an implication of those printed theorems. A later integral-forms paper treats broad almost-all-prime criteria rather than this uniform valuation-residue iff statement.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural density/non-density criterion for ternary diagonal cubic value quotients at every fixed p≠3, including a genuinely nontrivial mixed case in which a non-dense binary quotient becomes dense after adding one differently valued cubic term. The genus-one unit-surjectivity mechanism and exact coset closure are reusable local arithmetic tools.
residual_risks: Does not extend to prime three or general nondiagonal ternary cubics.

final_claim: For p!=3 and a,b,c nonzero integers, the quotient of values of aX^3+bY^3+cZ^3 is dense in Q_p iff p=2 mod3 or two coefficient valuations coincide modulo three; otherwise its closure is {0} plus 3 or 7 of the 9 cubic cosets, depending on whether abc is a p-adic cube.
